I've been farming this land for 30 years. I know Quzhou's soil and weather. I don't need to experiment — I need a good harvest. My kids help off-farm but the farm is still the backbone. Here's how I think through it.

**Wheat (planted this October, harvested next June):**
I'll put all 9.5 mu into wheat-maize rotation the same as every year. For wheat I'll buy Jimai-series improved seed from the township supply co-op — same as my neighbors, proven in this soil. I'll do a base fertilizer application at planting — compound fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium worked in — then top-dress urea at jointing stage in spring. Irrigation: I'll pump the well three times — once before winter freeze sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. I'll spray herbicide in early spring when weeds come up, then fungicide once for powdery mildew and rust, and one aphicide spray before harvest. I'll rotary till after maize harvest to incorporate the stubble before seeding wheat.

**Maize (planted June after wheat harvest, harvested September):**
I'll plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958, everyone around here uses it, yields are reliable. Base compound fertilizer at planting, then heavy urea top-dress at the 8-9 leaf stage when the plant is really pushing. Maize in summer usually gets some rain, so I'll only irrigate at planting if it's dry and again at silking if needed — maybe twice. One herbicide spray right after emergence, one more pesticide pass mid-season for corn borer if I see it. I'll rotary till after wheat harvest to level the field before planting.
